options: A T-SQL script library, not a PowerShell module
A Microsoft-only proprietary tool available only with Enterprise edition
A GUI application that replaces SQL Server Management Studio
A free, open-source PowerShell module, maintained by working DBAs, with hundreds of pre-built commands for SQL Server administration tasks
questions.explain: dbatools is a genuinely open-source, community-maintained PowerShell module built for real DBA automation tasks.

questions.q: What naming convention do dbatools commands follow?
options: Numbered commands like Command1, Command2
Random, unpredictable names with no shared pattern
Verb-DbaNoun, e.g. Get-DbaDatabase, Backup-DbaDatabase, Test-DbaLastBackup
All lowercase, snake_case names
questions.explain: The consistent Verb-DbaNoun pattern makes most command names genuinely guessable once you know the convention.

questions.q: Why does Test-DbaLastBackup actually restore the backup instead of just checking that the file exists?
options: This behavior is a bug that dbatools plans to remove
A file that exists on disk isn't proof it's actually restorable — an actual restore catches corruption or other issues a simple existence check would miss
Restoring is required by SQL Server licensing
It doesn't actually restore anything, just checks the file size
questions.explain: The whole value of the command is verifying the backup is genuinely usable, not just present.

questions.q: What does SMO refer to, in relation to dbatools?
options: A SQL Server edition tier
SQL Server Management Objects — the .NET API dbatools is partly built on
The name of dbatools' original author
A separate competing PowerShell module
questions.explain: SMO gives raw .NET objects for SQL Server administration; dbatools builds pre-tested, ready-to-use commands on top of that foundation.

questions.q: Why did dbatools largely replace DBAs' personal libraries of hand-rolled scripts, per this lesson?
options: There is no real reason — it's simply more popular
Personal scripts are illegal to use in production
dbatools is required by every SQL Server installation
It consolidates DBA automation into a single, community-tested module used and fixed by thousands of contributors, rather than untested, undocumented individual scripts
questions.explain: Wide real-world usage and many contributors mean bugs get found and fixed fast, unlike an individual DBA's untested personal scripts.
